resources.string: The app that wrote the sleep session, or any app that writes heart rate and steps.
Shorter sessions (after merging fragments) are ignored; longer ones below the nap threshold are processed as naps.
Fragments of one night from one app with a shorter gap become one night; the gap is written as awake.
How far back the history backfill goes; 0 = all available history.
Time of the daily run (approximate: Android may delay background work).
How often the background job asks Health Connect for new sleep sessions.
Only when the battery is not low
Background runs wait until the battery is not low.
Placeholders: {estimator}, {version}, {confidence}. Leave empty for the default title.

Skip up-to-date nights: nights already estimated with the current parameters are skipped, except that a recent night is updated when more heart-rate data arrives for it; nights estimated with other parameters are marked stale and recomputed only when you ask. Recompute everything: every run estimates the nights it reads again and rewrites their sessions, also for source sessions that already have sleep stages (recent sessions checked for late heart-rate data are rewritten only when their data changed). Never overwrite: an existing PulseStages session is never rewritten, not even by Recompute or when more heart-rate data arrives; only nights without a session are estimated.
For apps that show awakenings poorly. Changes the written data.
Hybrid (trained classifier + duration model) is the default; HMM and Rules are simpler alternatives.
Readings below are dropped as artefacts.
Readings above are dropped as artefacts.
Readings further than this many scaled MADs from the window median are replaced.
Lower bound of the filter\'s scale, so that 1-bpm steps in flat windows are kept.
Gaps up to this length are interpolated; longer gaps count as no data.
Median filter length in epochs, applied before smoothing (odd).
Heart rate is read this long before and after the session; stages are written only inside it.
Share of epochs with heart rate needed for the main estimator.
Between this and the minimum coverage the rules estimator is used; below it the night is skipped.
Sessions shorter than this are not estimated; 0 = off (sessions shorter than the minimum session length of the sources are ignored anyway).
hrNorm = (hr − P_low) / (P_high − P_low) over the night.
Upper percentile of the heart-rate normalization.
Smaller ranges are clamped and mark the night as low confidence.
hrVar is the standard deviation of the raw series within ± this many epochs.
hrSlope is the least-squares slope (bpm/min) within ± this many epochs.
Minimum distance between ultradian heart-rate minima.
Minimum depth of an ultradian heart-rate minimum.
Number of previous nights whose minima form the heart-rate baseline.
A night minimum above the baseline by more than this marks the night as elevated.
On elevated nights the awake threshold is raised by this amount of hrNorm.
Night confidence is multiplied by this on elevated nights.
Use blood-oxygen data when present and permitted.
Drop below the rolling night median (percentage points) counted as a desaturation.
Likelihood multiplier of awake and light in epochs with a desaturation.
Length of the rolling median that defines the SpO2 baseline.
Use RMSSD heart-rate variability when present and permitted.
Weight of the RMSSD-based variability feature when it replaces hrVar.
An epoch uses the nearest HRV sample only if it is at most this far away.
Use respiratory-rate data when present and permitted.
Weight of the respiratory-rate variability term.
Respiratory variability is the standard deviation within ± this many epochs.
Epochs at or below this hrNorm (with low variability) are deep sleep.
Epochs above this hrNorm are awake.
REM: earliest part of the night
REM is only allowed after this fraction of the night.
Probability given to the chosen stage (used by post-processing and the confidence).
How far proportion calibration moves the hrNorm thresholds; 0 = no calibration for the rules.
Gaussian emission of each state over hrNorm, hrVar and hrSlope: mean μ and standard deviation σ (σ > 0).
Mean bout length; sets the self-transition probability 1 − epoch / bout.
Shares of the transition mass that leaves a state; each row is normalized and zeros are replaced by ε.
Weight of awake in the initial distribution (deep and REM get ε).
Weight of light sleep in the initial distribution.
LIGHT→DEEP multiplier = max(floor, intercept − slope·t), t = fraction of the night.
How fast deep sleep becomes less likely during the night.
Lowest LIGHT→DEEP multiplier late in the night.
How fast REM becomes more likely during the night.
REM is suppressed during this many minutes after the session starts.
REM probability multiplier during the lockout.
Weight of the ultradian-cycle prior; 0 = off.
Cycle phase (0–1 between minima) at which the deep prior peaks.
Cycle phase at which the REM prior peaks.
This many steps in an epoch force awake.
Awake likelihood multiplier for fewer steps than the threshold.
Baum–Welch re-estimation of μ and σ per night, shrunk towards the table.
Shrinkage towards the emission table (epoch-equivalents per state).
Explicit gamma bout durations (HSMM) or geometric durations (plain HMM).
Weight of P(stage | time of night) relative to the class prior.
Longest bout the duration model considers.
Exponent of the classifier\'s scaled likelihoods (1 = as trained).
Exponent β of the class priors in the scaled likelihoods p(stage | x) / prior^β (1 = divide by the priors, 0 = raw posteriors, which favour light sleep).
Awake likelihood multiplier on nights with elevated heart rate.
Shorter deep bouts are merged into their neighbours.
Shorter REM bouts are merged into their neighbours.
Shorter awakenings are merged into their neighbours.
What to write for epochs inside long heart-rate gaps.
Epochs whose highest probability is below this are low confidence.
Keep the decoded stage or write light sleep.
The sanity check runs only on nights with more coverage than this.
More deep sleep than this share is implausible.
Less deep sleep than this share is implausible.
More REM sleep than this share is implausible.
Night confidence multiplier when a share is implausible.
Gently shift the stage priors until the shares fall inside the target ranges.
Share of the night the calibration aims at for deep sleep.
Share of the night the calibration aims at for REM sleep.
Largest share of awake the calibration accepts.
Use the personal model that Calibrate on the Compare tab fits on reference nights. With the HMM, also adapt to your nights every few weeks.
The population adaptation (EM) runs after this many newly estimated nights.
Shrinkage of the adaptation towards the global parameters.
How strongly calibrated values are pulled towards the global model.
Share of reference nights kept aside to report kappa before and after calibration.
Minimum level of the internal log (also mirrored to logcat).
